title: C# Questions & Answers - Structures
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on structures of C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the correct statement in the following C# code?

options.text: New structure can be inherited from struct book
When the program terminates, variable b will get garbage collected
The structure variable 'b' will be created on the stack
The structure variable 'b' will be created on the heap

questions.explanation: A local struct variable is a value-type local and is stored on the stack (or in a register). Structs cannot be inherited, and locals are not garbage-collected as objects.

questions.question: What will be the correct statement in the following C# code?

options.text: trial object referred by z is created on the stack
z is created on the heap
Both s and z will be created on the heap
s will be created on the stack

questions.explanation: s is a local struct, so it lives on the stack (or in a register). z is a reference-type field stored inside that struct; new sample() does not allocate a trial object, so z is null. A trial instance would live on the heap only after it is constructed.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about empty structures in C#?

options.text: C# does not allow empty structures
An empty structure is allowed and occupies at least 1 byte
An empty structure has size 0
Empty structures can only be declared as classes

questions.explanation: Empty structs compile in C#. Their size is at least 1 byte so each instance has a unique address.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about structures as to why they are defined as value types but not reference types?

options.text: Since space required for structure variables is allocated on stack which is a form of memory that is automatically available when a variable to be used is in scope
Structures generally are used to represent user defined data types that consists of small amount of data in them. Hence using stack for declaration of such variables is not a problem
All of the mentioned
None of the mentioned

questions.explanation: Local structs are value types and typically live on the stack while in scope. They are a good fit for small data. Boxed structs or struct fields of a class live on the heap with the object.

questions.question: Choose the wrong statement about structures in C#.NET?

options.text: Structures can be declared within a procedure
Structures can implement an interface but they cannot inherit from another structure
Structure members cannot be declared as protected
A structure is a value type

questions.explanation: A struct cannot be declared inside a method. Structs may implement interfaces, cannot inherit from another struct, cannot have protected members, and are value types.

questions.question: The correct way to define a variable of type struct abc in the following C# code?

options.text: abc e = new abc();
abc();

abc e;
e = new abc;
abc e = new abc;

questions.explanation: abc e = new abc(); constructs the struct. new abc without () is a syntax error.

questions.question: When does a structure variable get destroyed?

options.text: When no reference refers to it, it will get garbage collected
Depends on whether it is created using new or without new operator
As variable goes out of the scope
Depends on either we free its memory using free() or delete()

questions.explanation: A local struct is destroyed when it goes out of scope. It is not garbage-collected as a heap object unless boxed. C# has no free()/delete() for managed structs.

questions.question: Calculate the number of bytes a structure variable s occupies in the memory if it is defined as follows.

options.text: 24 bytes
8 bytes
16 bytes
12 bytes

questions.explanation: The struct contains int (4 bytes), Single (4 bytes), and a class reference (8 bytes on 64-bit), totaling 16 bytes. Marshal.SizeOf confirms 16 on a 64-bit runtime.

questions.question: Select the wrong statements among the following?

options.text: A structure can contain properties
A structure can contain constructors
A structure can contain protected data members
A structure can contain constants

questions.explanation: Structs cannot declare protected members because they do not support inheritance. They may have properties, constructors, and constants.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct result for the given statement in the C#.NET statement given below? p = q

options.text: Elements of 'q' will be copied into corresponding elements of p
Address stored in q will get copied into p
Address of first element of q will get copied into p
Once assignment is over. q will go out of scope and hence get exited forever

questions.explanation: Assigning one struct to another copies field values (value semantics), not a reference.
